From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary points

1. **The "FINAL" label and the claimed market norms are the Seller's advocacy, not agreed terms.** The preamble says these positions were "settled at principal level" and "not intended to be re-opened." Nothing in our record shows that. Please confirm with Wattlebridge principals before treating any point as closed. Until then, each one should be treated as open.
2. **The Seller Update contradicts its own Disclosure Letter.** The Update says Bluefen is "addressed," Riverlark will be "released" and DD-006 is "not material." The Disclosure Letter says no Bluefen consent has been delivered, the facility has not been repaid, and the incident's scope and whether it must be notified are unknown. We should rely on the Disclosure Letter facts, not the Update's descriptions.
3. **Several items are debt-like or are known risks.** In a debt-free/cash-free deal, these (Riverlark, the bonuses and possibly Sandbar) belong in the price mechanics or in specific indemnities. They should not sit inside the general warranty regime, where caps, the basket and disclosure would leave the Buyer with little or no remedy.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap (opening at 30–50%), or 20% only if W&I insurance sits behind it. Fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and fraud claims must sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. Do not accept 20% unless the carve-outs in N-004, N-005 and N-014 are agreed. *Reason: a 20% cap is only tolerable if the known risks are carved out of it.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket (about 1%), with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** A tipping basket (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). The basket should be around AUD 120k (0.5%). De minimis should be about AUD 10k, with related claims aggregated. No thresholds should apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. *Reason: a deductible basket combined with a high de minimis permanently removes AUD 250k+ of genuine loss from recovery.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. The Seller also wants every limitation to apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers two audit cycles. Separate, longer periods should apply to other claim types: fundamental (6–7 years or the statutory limitation period); tax (expiry of the ATO amendment period plus 6 months); IP (at least 3 years).
- **Recommendation:** Counter, and reject the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason: 18 months is short for SaaS revenue and IP issues, and the default rule would quietly cut back tax and title protection.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties get the same cap and time limit as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, with no de minimis or basket, no disclosure qualification and the longest available limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: if title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, so a 4.8m cap is not a credible remedy.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 (limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out. None of the limitations, the exclusive-remedy clause or the non-reliance clause should apply to fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their representatives. The carve-out should also preserve statutory rights where they cannot be excluded (for example, misleading or deceptive conduct claims under ACL s 18).
- **Recommendation:** Insist. *Reason: this is non-negotiable market protection, and the current drafting arguably shields fraud.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). Clause 1.4 also disclaims any admission of materiality or legal requirement.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosures only, made "fairly," meaning in enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific disclosures should be set against specific warranties. Disclosures must not qualify fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. At most, accept named data room documents to the extent fairly disclosed. *Reason: general disclosure lets the Seller qualify every warranty with the entire data room.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause and add a pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge does not reduce claims except to the extent fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. *Reason: "discoverable" and "advisers" together create constructive knowledge that would wipe out most claims.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. The Disclosure Letter confirms no consent has been obtained and the clause 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent requiring unconditional written consent under clause 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer. The clause 11.3 conditions must be evidenced as satisfied. The Seller should use best (or all reasonable) endeavours, and only the Buyer should be able to waive the condition. If the condition is not met by the sunset date, the Buyer can terminate.
- **Recommendation:** Insist. *Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m), so losing it would undermine the valuation.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion." About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the facility has a change-of-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2).
- **Buyer wants:** The facility treated as Debt and repaid from the price through the funds flow at Completion. A payoff letter and deed of release must be delivered at Completion. PPSR and any share security must be discharged. There should be no change-of-control default exposure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. *Reason: under a debt-free deal, Completion would otherwise trigger a default on a live secured facility that the Buyer then owns.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420k is "a matter for the Seller," yet it is not in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses plus all on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG administration) treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt and deducted from the price. They should be paid through Company payroll at Completion, backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Insist. *Reason: the Company is the employer and will bear the cost, so leaving it out of the funds flow shifts at least AUD 420k to the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent requiring evidence of cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, a broad specific indemnity covering any loss from the Company not owning or not being free to use the SOW3 Project Materials. It should sit outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure, and be supported by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. *Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership does not pass until every fee is paid, so the real risk is to the IP itself, not just the AUD 180k.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter admits that access, scope and whether notification is required are all unknown for about 1,240 personal records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before Completion: a completed forensic investigation and a documented Notifiable Data Breaches (NDB) assessment under the Privacy Act. The Act expects that assessment within 30 days, and the Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September, so we should ask whether it has been done.
  - Any notifications required should be made before Completion.
  - A specific indemnity covering regulator action and penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, with an escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Insist. *Reason: the incident is known but unquantified, so the Seller should carry it rather than relying on disclosure to shift it to the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are said to be ordinary-course costs. The Disclosure Letter itself says to "read together," and does not say whether they are avoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies of the renewals and confirmation of their term, termination rights and whether they are at arm's length.
  - The three treated as one commitment for any conduct-of-business consent threshold (check whether splitting kept each below that threshold).
  - Any amount that is unaccrued and not ordinary course treated as a liability in the price, or covered by a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller's characterisation. *Reason: related renewals of identical size suggest one AUD 330k commitment presented in pieces.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Clearly defined claim categories, each with its own regime: General Warranty, Fundamental Warranty, Tax Warranty/Indemnity, IP Warranty, Specific Indemnity and Fraud. The general limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims, expressly.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default. *Reason: as drafted, every carve-out the Buyer wins could be undone by the catch-all rule.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Relies only on the DD-012 share register. The Disclosure Letter confirms the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent checks: an ASIC company extract, share certificates, the constitution, any options or convertibles, and a PPSR search, specifically checking for any Riverlark security over the shares.
  - Title as a fundamental warranty.
  - Completion deliverables: signed transfers, certificates, releases of any share security, and officer resignations.
- **Recommendation:** Insist. *Reason: a register maintained by the Seller is not independent evidence of unencumbered title.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, capped at 100% of price, with no thresholds and running to the end of the ATO amendment period plus 6 months. IP warranties should have a longer limitation period and potentially a higher cap.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open, not settled. *Reason: placing tax and IP under the 20%/18-month regime would leave the key SaaS and tax exposures largely unprotected.*

---

## Suggested next steps
1. Confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether anything was actually agreed at principal level.
2. Send a mark-up that resets the claim categories (N-014) first, since most other points depend on it.
3. Send supplementary DD requests: Bluefen correspondence, the Riverlark payoff figure, the Ironquay payment evidence, the DD-006 forensic report and NDB assessment, the Sandbar contracts, and ASIC/PPSR searches.
4. Consider W&I insurance. Note that known matters (DD-004, DD-005, DD-006, DD-003) will be excluded from W&I cover, which reinforces the need for specific indemnities and an escrow.
